{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Software License and Maintenance Agreement (Garman / Sparkling)

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement
**Status:** All findings below verified.

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Software License and Maintenance Agreement. The overall risk profile is mixed but workable: the agreement is unusually clean on several fronts that often cost us leverage, and the remaining problems are concentrated in a small number of high-value items.

What is already acceptable and requires no redline: the Vendor-side IP indemnity in Section 13 (uncapped, with procure/replace/modify remedies, and expressly excluded from the Section 15 damages limitation); the absence of any exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-commitment, liquidated-damages or audit obligation binding us; our unconditional 90-day termination-for-convenience right in Section 17(b) with no exit charge; the absence of auto-renewal (maintenance is a "renewable one-year term"); and the Section 12 warranty, which runs for the acceptance period plus one year and continues while the Software remains under Maintenance Services, with a repair remedy and a full-refund rejection right, and with no "AS IS" or implied-warranty disclaimer anywhere in the document.

Where we need to negotiate, there are three critical or near-critical items. First, **Section 15 contains no monetary cap at all** — direct damages are open-ended for both parties, including for us — which fails our fallback of a mutual twelve-month fee cap. Second, **Section 13 vests ownership of the entire Work in Garman, expressly including the Schedule "D" Modifications we commission and pay for**, and the agreement is silent on ownership of our data. Third, **Sections 20(d) and 3(c) impose a blanket assignment bar with no affiliate or M&A successor carve-out for us and no reasonableness standard on consent** — walk-away territory for a customer change-of-control event, and the same defect narrows the licence grant in Section 2. Beyond those, governing law sits in the Vendor's home jurisdiction (Nova Scotia/Canada, non-exclusive venue), Section 19 is a mutual **no-hire** covering all employees rather than a targeted non-solicit, and the agreement omits post-termination transition assistance and return of our data, as well as any vendor insurance covenant.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Page 6 (Section 13) | Vendor IP indemnity covering Losses, settlement and reasonable legal fees, plus procure/replace/modify remedies; not capped, as Section 15 excludes Section 13. At or above fallback. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Intellectual Property Indemnity | Garman owns the whole Work including the Schedule "D" Modifications; no title passes to us; agreement silent on ownership of our data. Fails preferred and fallback. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 15 Limitation of Garman's Liability | Mutual exclusion of indirect damages and Section 13/14 carve-outs, but **no monetary cap whatsoever**; fails the fallback twelve-month mutual cap. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | Page 10 (Section 20(d)) | Blanket mutual assignment bar, no affiliate/M&A successor carve-out for us, no reasonableness standard; reinforced one-sidedly by Section 3(c). Walk-away territory. |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 2 Grant of License | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; licence grants are non-exclusive; Section 3 contains ordinary scope limits only. |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | No liquidated damages, penalty, minimum fee or early-termination charge; Section 17(b) exit is fee-free. |
| 7 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No non-compete or field-of-use restraint; Section 14 preserves an independent-development carve-out. |
| 8 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 17 Term and Termination | Unconditional 90-day convenience right for us with no exit charge; Garman has no convenience right. Sits at fallback on the notice period. |
| 9 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Restrictions on Use | No audit, inspection or verification right over us anywhere; the only examination right (Section 16 escrow) runs in our favour. |
| 10 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | Page 10 (§ 20(h)) | Nova Scotia/Canadian law, Nova Scotia courts — Vendor's home jurisdiction and outside the accepted list. Non-exclusive venue keeps it short of walk-away. |
| 11 | Medium | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of License | Perpetual and affiliate-covering (good), but expressly "non-transferable" with no successor carve-out and no coverage for contractors. Fails fallback on transferability. |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No MFN or best-terms mechanic in either direction; pricing simply refers to the Fee Schedule. |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 11 Fees | No minimum, take-or-pay or shortfall obligation; fees payable for the licence and services actually taken; maintenance is a one-year renewable term. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 19 Non-Solicitation of Employees | Mutual **no-hire** (not non-solicit) covering all employees of the other party and affiliates, with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 10 Maintenance and Support | No automatic renewal; renewal requires agreement. Absence of a maintenance uplift cap noted only. |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 17 Term and Termination | Post-termination obligations run one way only (we return Garman's materials). No obligation on Garman to return our data or provide exit assistance; not in the Section 18 survival list. |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 12 Specifications and Warranty | Conformance warranty for acceptance period plus one year and while under Maintenance Services, with repair remedy and rejection/full-refund right; no implied-warranty disclaimer. Exceeds preferred. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 20 General Matters | No insurance covenant anywhere, despite Garman attending our Authorized Locations (Section 4) and converting our data (Section 4(b)). |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

Two findings reach walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as non-negotiable in substance:

1. **Assignment / change of control (Finding 4 — § 20(d), reinforced by § 3(c) and the "non-transferable" licence in § 2).** A blanket consent requirement with no affiliate or successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard is walk-away territory for a customer M&A event. Helpfully, Section 17 contains no change-of-control termination right for Garman, and our redline preserves that expressly.
2. **Section 19 no-hire (Finding 14).** No-hire provisions, and restrictions reaching all vendor personnel rather than those involved in the services, are each walk-away items under the rule. Because the mutual structure is part of the bargain, we have narrowed to the fallback rather than deleting the clause.

For completeness on items that stop short of walk-away: the governing-law deviation (Finding 10) fails both preferred and fallback but the venue is non-exclusive rather than an exclusive foreign forum; and the missing insurance covenant (Finding 18) engages the playbook's walk-away scenario only if the Vendor both attends our premises and processes our data uninsured — which is why we are inserting the covenant rather than accepting silence.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Liability cap (Finding 3, critical).** Insert the preferred mutual cap — greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 — with uncapped Excluded Claims (indemnification, confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), retaining the existing Section 13/14 carve-out and confirming our fee payment obligations are not capped damages. We can note internally that "fees" is undefined but set by the Fee Schedule (Section 11), so the cap basis is the full licence and maintenance stream.
2. **IP and data ownership (Finding 2, critical).** Add a carve-out to Section 13 confirming we retain all rights in our data and pre-existing IP, and confirm the Section 2 licence extends to Improvements and Modifications. We are not disturbing Garman's ownership of its underlying software.
3. **Assignment and licence transferability (Findings 4 and 11).** Add an affiliate/successor carve-out for us with a reasonableness standard and no-competitor limit on Garman assignments, expressly confirm our change of control gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right, and extend the Section 2 licence to contractors acting on our behalf with a successor-transfer right overriding Sections 3(c) and 20(d). These two redlines should be presented together as one package.
4. **Governing law (Finding 10).** Replace Nova Scotia/Canada with New York law and exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, flagging Delaware, California, or England and Wales as acceptable fallbacks.
5. **Non-solicitation (Finding 14).** Convert to a mutual twelve-month solicitation-only restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the services, measured from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
6. **Transition assistance (Finding 16).** Insert a new Section 17(d): up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of our data in machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter. Fallback available at 90 days' assistance plus 30-day data export.
7. **Insurance (Finding 18).** Insert a new Section 20(j): CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our data is processed, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M to be offered in the comment.
8. **Commercial follow-ups (no redline).** Raise with the business team, outside the legal markup: the absence of any cap on maintenance fee uplift at renewal (preferred is the lesser of CPI and 3%) if the Fee Schedule permits unilateral increases; whether a Garman-granted MFN in our favour is obtainable; and the ten-day claim-notice period and absence of an express duty to defend under the Section 13 indemnity, which we are not flagging as deviations but may trade for elsewhere."}
